html:
The migration of Japanese families to Brazil, which began on 18 June 1908 when the ship Kasato Maru landed about 780 migrants at the port of Santos. Japanese migration peaked between the late 1920s and mid 1930s.

Brazil needed workers for the coffee farms of São Paulo after the end of slavery and a fall in Italian migration. Japan had crowded farmland and, after 1924, the US closed its doors to Japanese migrants. The first arrivals found hard work and low pay on the plantations. Over time many bought land of their own and became small farmers, growing vegetables, tea, cotton and fruit, and later moved to the cities.

During World War II Brazil sided with the Allies and restricted the Japanese community. After the war, a secret society that refused to believe Japan had lost attacked those who accepted it. Today Brazil has about 2 million people of Japanese descent, the largest such community outside Japan, centred on São Paulo's Liberdade district. From the 1990s many moved to Japan to work.
sum: The migration of Japanese families to Brazil, which began on 18 June 1908 when the ship Kasato Maru landed about 780 migrants at the port of Santos. Japanese migration peaked between the late 1920s and mid 1930s.
